Record type: official course catalog overview.
Course: CS300 - Data Structures.
SU credits: 3.
ECTS: 6.
Engineering ECTS: 5.
Basic science ECTS: 1.
Prerequisites: CS 204 - Undergraduate - Min Grade D.
Corequisites: CS 300R.
Description: This course covers some of the fundamental data structures  as well as the algorithms operating on them. Topics  included are: Introduction to theoretical aspects of  computing: modeling algorithms and their run times,  computational complexity. Linear data structures (lists,  stacks, queues), trees (binary search trees, AVL trees, tree  traversals), hash tables, priority queues, disjoint sets,  sorting algorithms, graphs and their representations, graph  algorithms (depth first and breadth first search, single  source shortest path algorithms), sorting algorithms,  algorithmic paradigms (divide and conquer, greedy,  dynamic programming).

9. Putting It All Together: The Full Encoder Layer
Each of BERT’s 12 (or 24) encoder layers follows this exact sequence:
Multi-Head Self-Attention: Q, K, V projections → 12 parallel attention heads → concatenate → output projection Wᴼ
Residual Connection + LayerNorm₁: Add the input back and normalize
Feed-Forward Network: Linear₁ (768 → 3072) → GELU → Linear₂ (3072 → 768)
Residual Connection + LayerNorm₂: Add the input back and normalize
This block is repeated 12 times (BERT-Base) or 24 times (BERT-Large). The input to encoder 1 comes from the embedding layer; all subsequent encoders take their input from the encoder directly below.

1. The Transformer Architecture
The Transformer was introduced by Vaswani et al. in the 2017 paper "Attention Is All You Need." It replaced slow recurrent neural networks (RNNs/LSTMs) with a purely attention-based architecture, enabling massive parallelization during training.
The original Transformer has two main components:
Encoder: Reads the entire input sequence at once and produces context-rich representations. Used by BERT.
Decoder: Generates output tokens one at a time, attending to both the encoder’s output and its own previously generated tokens. Used by GPT.
